Guides

How much does a website cost? The real price, no surprises

The price of a website does not stop at building it. There is what you pay once, and what you pay for as long as the site exists. Here is how to add it all up before you sign.

The two parts of the price

A website is a bit like a car: there is the purchase price, then insurance, fuel and servicing. Many bad surprises come from only looking at the first number.

What you pay once: building the site, meaning its design, its text, its layout and putting it online.

What you pay every year or every month:

  • The domain name: the site's address, rented by the year.
  • Hosting: the computer that runs day and night, keeps your site and sends it to visitors.
  • Updates: a site that is not maintained ends up breaking down or getting hacked.
  • Changes: opening hours, a price, a photo. They are often charged by the hour.

Questions to ask before you sign

Whoever you choose, always ask:

  1. Are the domain name and hosting included? For how long?
  2. Who does the updates, and at what price?
  3. How much does a small change cost?
  4. Is there a minimum commitment?
  5. What happens if I stop?

A quote that does not answer these five questions is not complete.

My prices, in full

With me, there is only one build price, shown before you order:

  • One-page website or showcase website up to five pages: €500
  • Online shop: €700, which is €200 more

You pay 25% when you order, and the rest when the site goes live. The rest can be spread over 6 or 12 months at no extra cost.

After that, a single subscription covers everything recurring: €10 a month. It is required, but with no commitment. Here is what it includes:

  • The domain name, in your name, and hosting.
  • Updates, backups and website monitoring.
  • Support, with a reply within 72 hours.
  • The SEO basics.
  • Every month, 100 Lia Tokens and one change made by Alex.

One Lia Token is worth one cent. Your tokens pay for the changes Lia makes to your website, between 30 and 65 tokens each, and for the tools in your client area.

Three examples over the first year

  • A tradesperson with a one-page website: €500 + 12 × €10 = €620.
  • A shop with a showcase website and the Ongoing SEO extra: €500 + 12 × (€10 + €10) = €740.
  • A maker with an online shop: €700 + 12 × €10 = €820.

In the following years, only the subscription remains. If you pay it yearly, you get 2 months free: €100 instead of €120.

Why these prices are low

It is not a cut-price website. Built by hand by an agency or a freelancer, a showcase website usually costs between €1,500 and €3,000. Mine costs 4 to 5 times less, and the difference comes from the method: Lia, my AI assistant, prepares the text, layout and settings in a few hours instead of several days. I read, correct and check everything before it goes live. The my method page explains what each of us does.

What can push the bill up

To be clear, here is what is not in the base price.

When your website is built, some options are paid once: English translation (€100), Appointment booking (€100), Moving your old website (€100), Five more pages (€100).

Then, extras can be added to the subscription if you need them, and removed whenever you like: Ongoing SEO (€10 a month), Lia + (€5 a month), Detailed figures (€5 a month), Business email address (€3 a month).

You put it all together on the create my website page, and the total updates as you go.

Your questions

Is there such a thing as a free website?

Some tools let you publish a page without paying, but with an address that carries the tool's name and often adverts. For a business, an address in your own name is better, and it is never free.

Why do prices vary so much from one provider to another?

Because the time spent is not the same. A site designed from scratch by a team takes weeks of work. A site built on a proven base, with the help of AI, takes much less. Both approaches are valid, for different needs.

Do I have to pay everything at once?

No. You pay 25% when you order. The rest is due when the site is live, in one go or in 6 or 12 monthly payments at no extra cost.
